I mean, today, unfortunately, we lost a quarter of an hour before we started because the previous case that was sitting in the morning overstayed in the courtroom by 15 minutes and, therefore, the 15 minutes were taken from our time. We lost time in the beginning because of other procedural matters. We lost time because of this incident. I even doubt whether Ms. Sellers will be able to finish today. I don't know. But that's the position. So while yesterday we were quite adamant and tried to impress on you the need to finish by Friday, we have to be flexible now. Justice comes first, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Absolutely. And that's all the more reason why we need full proofing notes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Trevisan, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Again, Mr. Petrovic, my apologies to you, but Madam Prosecutor and the Defence today have decided to raise some issues that needed to be resolved before we continue with your testimony. They are procedural matters. Nothing to do with you. Absolutely nothing to do with you. Yes, Ms. Sellers, please, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, might I turn your attention to the latter part of 1992, the month of December. Did there come a time period when the village of Bjelovac was attacked?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: On what day was the village attacked?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: 14th of December, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And at what time did the attack begin? What time of day?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Early in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Could you please describe for the Trial Chamber how the attack occurred, but more specifically, what you did and what you saw during the attack.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: On the 14th December 1992, I slept in my house, and my house is 100 metres from the main road that goes through Bjelovac. Very close to the Drina River. I was awoken by shooting. I got up. I was alone at home. My wife and my children were in Serbia, in Grabovica. I got up and I went out to see what was going on. When I got out I started walking towards the road. I felt shots behind me. I ran through the corn field to my sister's house. I entered my sister's house. There was shooting coming from all directions. I didn't know at the time who was behind my back, in the direction of Drina, where my house was. I was sitting in my sister's house and there was a window facing my house and I was observing what was going on. Below the garage of my house, I saw three uniformed persons appear first. They were followed by two people in civilian clothes. One of them was in a checkered red shirt and had a hat on his head. They came up to my house. They entered the house. They stayed there a few minutes, between five and fifteen minutes. I looked again and I saw smoke coming from my house, which means that they had set the house on fire. They left the house. They were taking their time. They returned the same way they came from, towards the Drina. The house was burning for some 15 or 20 minutes. Only one room actually burned down. The fire did not spread to the entire house. The first floor did not burn on that day. Then I realised that they, the Muslims, had arrived from the direction of the Drina River. I spent the entire day in the house, observing from my sister's house what was going on. I could see them entering the stables of Dusan Petrovic, who is my neighbour. There were some dozen people and there were a lot of heads that could be seen below a hedge or behind the hedge. I couldn't recognise anybody. But I did see when they set the house on fire and I knew that they were Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, let me just take you back to a couple of points that you've testified about. You said that you went to your sister's house. How far from your house was your sister's house located?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: 80 to 100 metres.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, is your sister's house, from your sister's house, are you able to clearly see what you testified about as your garage and your house?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. One can clearly see it, because it is on the same plot of land.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, you stated it was early in the morning. Was it dark outside or was it light outside when you saw the people entering your house?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: It was light, because the day had already broken.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, you stated that some of the people who entered your house were in uniform and some were dressed in what appeared to be civilian clothes. Could you tell the Trial Chamber what types of uniforms that you saw, the people who entered your house?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Three of them wore camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Were the people who entered your house, both the uniformed and the non-uniformed, were they carrying weapons of any kind?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Did they enter your house together or did they appear to enter the house together?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: First the three of them got in an then the other two followed. I was able to see that because the entrance to the house looks directly at the place from which I was observing the scene.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: When you say that the three of them went into the house first, were those the people in uniform or were they the people in the civilian clothing?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: The first three that got in wore uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, did the people in uniforms try and prevent the people in civilian clothing from entering into your house?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: No. The other two got in, too.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, you've testified that you saw smoke coming up and then that your house was burning. Did you see the people who went into your house, both the uniform people and the people in civilian clothes, leave your house?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Did they leave your house in a manner that could be described as calmly, or did they run out of the house frightened and fearful, possibly because of the fire?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: They did not run. They went out calmly and they went the way that went below the garage.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, just to clarify for the Trial Chamber. We've discussed the town of Bjelovac. Is your house on the section of Bjelovac between the road and the river, or between the road and the hills?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: It is between the road and the river.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And can you tell the Trial Chamber whether the people who came to your house came from the direction of the river or came from the direction of the hills?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: They had come from the direction of the Drina River and they went back the same way, towards the river.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, you've testified that you stayed at your sister's house during that day. Did you see any other incidences of burning that day while you were at your sister's house?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Later on perhaps an hour later, because I did not really look at my watch to see what the time was, I looked at the Sikirici and Jovanovici, and I could see that smoke was coming out of the houses, that's the houses were on fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now would you turn to the map next to you and you've already indicated -- indicated where Sikirici is. Could you please show the Trial Chamber where Jovanovici is?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Sikirici, this is here. And Jovanovici is here, close to Sikirici. There is only a small stream between them. They're bordering on each other. And then here, next to this wood here, wooded area here, there is the village of Jovanovici. This is here.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Could you please put a circle around that also, with the initials, the village of Jovanovici?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]. This is the river Loznica, and this is where Bjelovac starts. Jovanovici is here, in this area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For the record, the witness indicates a spot at the tip of the oblong shape that he has marked on the map indicating where the village of Jovanovici is, in the proximity of Sikirici.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now when you were observing burning from Jovanovici, would you please tell the Trial Chamber what did you specifically observe; what was burned; to your knowledge, how was it burned; and in what order, if any, was it burned.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, the house us houses below the wooded area started burning. They were also away from the road. First, Petro Jovanovic's house started burning. Then Milos, Milenko, and another person by the name of Jovanovic, they started burning. You could see the smoke coming out of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Did they all burn at the same time or did they burn one after another?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: One after the other. First one, then the other one. The second one. The third one. The fourth one.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Were you able to see whether the houses were hit by mortar shells? Or whether the houses had been set on fire by human beings?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: They were set on fire by human beings.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber why you say that, please.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, because they set fire to the houses by hand. They did not fire any mortars on them or anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, were you able to observe, from your sister's house, any other houses being set on fire that day, in Bjelovac, during the attack?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, I can't really be specific about the time. Houses on the other side of the road began burning, too. It may have been around noon or one p.m., I cannot be really specific about the time. But the houses of Mile Petrovic, Drago Filipovic, Stevo Filipovic, Milenko Vucetic, Slavko Martic as far as I can remember, those houses started to burn. And this is as far as they went burning houses on that day. They did not burn any other houses on that day.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: To clarify a bit, when you talked about the houses burning from Jovanovici, were those the houses above the road going toward the hills?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you. And this last group of houses that you've mentioned, houses of Mile Petrovic, Filipovic, were those the houses on the side of the road going toward the Drina River?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Down to the Drina River.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, were all of those houses, those on both sides of the road that you've testified that were burned, those are houses that are located closer to Sikirici than houses in Bjelovac that would be located to the other side of the town, toward Zaluzje, going toward Bratunac; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, it's closer to Sikirici.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, is your house located in the part of the town near Sikirici? Or is it located in the other end of the town going toward Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: It is located right in the middle of the village, in the middle of Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: So when you testified that only half or one-half of the village burned, were those houses starting from your house going back towards Sikirici?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: No. From Sikirici towards my house.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Certainly. Fine. Now, during the attack, while you were at your sister's house, did you hear the sounds of bullets, guns or other weapons?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, sure I did. Because you could hear shooting from all over the place. Both sides were shooting.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, were the village guards defending the village of Bjelovac at that time?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, they had pulled out towards the area in the middle of the village, because when the lines were broken through, they moved, they pulled out to that part of the village that had not yet fallen, those who survived the initial attack.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, you testified earlier that there were about, I believe, 30 or 40 members of the village guard. Were those 30 or 40 members fighting that morning during the attack, against the attackers?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm sure they fought.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Did you hear any other sounds, other than weapons, the sounds of human voices that day during the attack?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, I heard the people shouting from the woods and banging some metal objects. I don't know what it was. I couldn't really tell what it was. There was just a lot of noise. I don't know whether they did it in order to create panic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Did you, by any chance, hear what they were shouting, what the persons were shouting, the people were shouting?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, in that noise, you could hear them shout from the woods, "Allahu Akbar." They were just trying to create panic because they were banging those cans and other metal objects.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, could you tell the Trial Chamber how many people dressed in uniform and civilians with the people in uniform that was attacking the village that you saw that morning of the attack.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, I cannot really give you the exact number, that's impossible, because I didn't see all of them. But on the basis of the area from which they attacked, because it was a fairly large area, I can assume that they -- their numbers were large.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And when you say "large," do you mean more than 50?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, more. Much more.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: How many more would you estimate that their numbers were?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, quite a few of them, because they attacked a large area. I think 300, 500, up to 1.000. I cannot be specific about the figure. It was impossible. One could not see all of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And would it be your testimony that, in terms of the village guards, there were in between 30 and 40 people on duty that morning?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes. 30 to 50. There were seven trenches and you would have three to four people per trench. That would be the number for the village guards.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I could stop at this moment and continue after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. In fact, I was going to draw your attention to the time. We will have a 25-minute break, starting from now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, let's continue, Ms. Sellers, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, you testified that there were approximately, between 30 and 40 people on duty that morning and you said, well, maybe -- I'm sorry, 30 to 50.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Fifty.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Fifty, yes. I would like to ask you now, during the period of the attack that morning, did you hear any airplanes or type of helicopter or aviation machinery, or equipment?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: That was not in the morning. And an airplane appeared in the afternoon. I don't know exactly when. I believe that it was between 1.00 and 2.00 in the afternoon. Not in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Were you wearing a watch that morning of the attack, Mr. Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: No. I never wear a watch.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Did you have the opportunity to look at a clock on several occasions that morning during the attack?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: No. I did not pay any attention to the time of day.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: So were you telling the time of day more or less by whether it was light outside or whether it was dark outside?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Are you now referring to the airplane? Or to the attack on Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: To the attack on Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: The attack started early in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And throughout the day, did you just notice whether it was light outside or whether it was dark outside in order to indicate whether it was morning, evening, or night?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: The attack started in the morning and lasted the whole day, until 3.00 or half past 3.00 in the afternoon, maybe.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, getting back to the plane. Do you know from which direction the plane originally came?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: It came from the direction of Bratunac, up the stream of the Drina River.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And to your knowledge, during the attack, did the plane drop any detonation mechanisms or bombs or mortars or any other type of shells?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: As far as I could hear, there were two louder detonations that could not have been caused by simple shooting. I believe that something was dropped.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And did you see any craters that would have indicated detonation, craters or bomb craters in the town of Bjelovac at a later date?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: On the following day, on the 15th, when we returned in order to pick up the casualties, below the house of Radojka Damljanovic, there was a crater two metres wide and half a metre deep. I did not see the other crater. I only saw one crater. And I believe that this is what caused the damage to that house, because on the 14th, this house had not been set fire to.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: So it's your testimony that the bomb created the burning or the fire damage to that house, is that true?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: That house was never on fire. The only thing that I saw was this crater next to it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: So the bombing of the detonation did not cause that house to catch fire or to appear to be destroyed by fire, is that your correct testimony, correct characterisation of your testimony?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: The shell or whatever you want to call it, did not set the house on fire. It just damaged the walls and the roof fell off the house. The house was not set on fire on the 14th of December. Whatever damage there was, was probably caused by the detonation by this shell that created the crater.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Petrovic, you've testified that there were houses on the road above the road going toward the hills and houses on the road below going toward the river that were burning. And your testimony was that they had been set on fire. Did you see the airplane or an airplane dropping any bombs or detonation devices over these houses when you saw them being set on fire?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: I could not see that. I could only hear the detonations. I could not see them.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Did you hear those detonations when the houses of the Jovanovics and Filipovics were beginning to burn?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: No, no. That was later. That was in the afternoon. The house -- the houses burnt earlier on.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, did there come a time, during the attack that day, when the attacking forces -- what you've characterized or described as the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Muslims -- when they left Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: After the flight of the aircraft, they withdrew towards --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness repeat the names of the villages.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It could be in the afternoon, towards the end of the day. I don't know the exact time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, the interpreters didn't catch the names of the villages that you mentioned in your answer. Could you repeat them, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: They retreated towards which villages, please?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Pirici and Poloznik.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And are those the village [sic] that you marked earlier on the -- that is beside you?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Neighbouring villages. They are marked on the map.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And are those Muslim villages or Serb villages?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Muslim villages.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, did there come a time during that day, the 14th of December, when Serb forces came to assist the villagers in Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. After that aircraft flew over, some men that called themselves "the guards," arrived.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Did those men who called themselves the guards, then engage in fighting with the Muslim forces that were in Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Not on that day. They arrived late. The Muslim forces had already retreated.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, when you left your sister's house -- well let me ask you this. Did you leave your sister's house after the retreat of the Muslim forces?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: I went to my house.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Did you go to your house with anyone or did you go there by yourself?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: My brother was with me.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And when you went to your house, would you tell the Trial Chamber what you saw, what was the condition of your house.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: I entered the house. On the 14th, only one room burnt down. And the living room had been ransacked. However, the fire did not spread to either the living room or the floors -- or the rooms on the first floor. Only one room burnt down on the 14th of December.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, were you ever compensated or given reparations or somehow restitution for the burning of that one floor in your house that occurred on the 14th of December 1992?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: No. I did not receive anything. I used my own resources to repair my house. I have not completed the reparations. I have only repaired two rooms, so that I can live in them. The rest still remains as it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, where did you spend the night of the 14th of December, 1992, after the attack?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: The 14th of December?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: I spent the night in Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Did you spend the night in your house or did you spend the night in another house?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Not in my house. In my sister's house. My house was still burning and I didn't stay there. I went to my sister's place.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And did you stay in Bjelovac on the 15th, the next day, in the town? And if you did, would you tell the Trial Chamber what you did during at that day.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: On the 15th, we gathered, all of us villagers of Bjelovac gathered. There were a lot of casualties. We had to gather the bodies and bury them. On that day, on the 15th, I can state that not a single bullet was fired from the Muslim side. They allowed us to collect our bodies in peace.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, about how many people, to your knowledge, were killed in that attack?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Between 60 and 70.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, were the majority of bodies that you recovered, were they on the part of Bjelovac that is between the road and the river? Or were they on the part of Bjelovac that is between the road and the hills?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Most of them were between the road and the river, closer to the Drina. I suppose that they were fleeing towards the Drina, and then whatever happened there, happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Tell the Trial Chamber where, if any where, that the bodies were transported to on that day.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: They were transported to Serbia, by boat. We couldn't go through Zaluzje and Voljevica. That is why we transported them over the bridge to Bratunac and we buried them there on the 16th of December, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, did you return to Bjelovac on the 15th -- I'm sorry on the 16th of December?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Did any of the villagers in Bjelovac return to Bjelovac on the 16th of December or the 17th, or the time period close thereafter?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: On the 17th of December, as far as I know, an order was issued from Bratunac for the rest of the forces that had remained in Bjelovac to retreat.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, when you say the rest of the forces, are you referring to those guards who came down to assist you? Or are you referring to the inhabitants of Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mostly the guards, because the villagers of Bjelovac were no longer there because there was not a single house or a single household in which there was not at least one casualty.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now on the 16th and 17th of December, 1992, were you in Grabovica on the Serb side of the Drina River?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: On the 16th of December I was in Bratunac, attending the burial and then I returned to Grabovica, where my family was. On the 17th I returned.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, on that day, on the 17th, did you have the opportunity to look back across the river into your village of Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Would you please tell the Trial Chamber what you saw as you looked across the Drina River into the village.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: On that day, the 17th and the 18th and after that, again Muslims entered the village and the rest of the houses that were not burned on the 14th were set fire to on the 17th and 18th of December.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: So are you talking about the houses now that would be between your house and going in the direction of Bratunac? Or Zaluzje?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Those that were not set on fire on the 14th, the ones towards Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And please tell the Trial Chamber why you testified that the Muslims set the houses on fire on that day, the 17th and the 18th.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Because there were no Serb forces in Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to show Prosecution Exhibit 316. It's approximately six minutes. We will try and see if we can just move to a couple sections in it, in the interest of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So ...

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I believe it is up on Sanctions now. Mr. Petrovic I would ask you to look at the screen in front of you and we are going to run a video and I will ask you some questions concerning it as it runs.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, can you recognise anything in this video at this point?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Those are the houses in Bjelovac belonging to the Jovanovic family. As far as I can tell from the still.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Pardon me. Is that house those houses appeared when you saw them burning on the 14th of December, 1992?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I just want to indicate that we're on 20 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. For the record, the still from the video that the witness is being referred to is at 26 minutes 39.6 seconds. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Let's continue, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, can you indicate what this image is in front of you now.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: This is the Bjelovac school. And next to it is Bozo Rjumsevic's [phoen] house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And next to it, which side, left or right, Mr. Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On my left. And the big building is the primary school. This is the school, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. For the record, the witness is referring to a still from the video that occurs at 27.03.2.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Petrovic, is it your testimony that the school and these houses were not burned on the 14th, but that they were burned on the 17th? I believe the 16th or 17th, at a later date?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Later. Later. Not on the 14th. This is the part of the village that remained standing on the 14th.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you. We can continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, in the front centre of this picture, there seems to be a very small white structure. Do you recognise what that small white squared structure is?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: I do recognise it. These are the pools for the water supply system for Bratunac, the wells, that's what we call them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For the record, the witness is referring to a still from the video which occurs at 27 minutes 08 seconds, point 7.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, did the village guard, guard at times what you've described as the pools for the water supply to Bratunac, such as the one we're seeing on our screen now?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, the water supply system is behind the backs of the guards, but there would always be a soldier or two at the building where the pools are located.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you. We can continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, is this the airplane that you saw on the 14th of December, 1992 during the attack on Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: I think, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, the sound that we've just heard while this picture was running, is that similar to the sound of the airplane that you heard on that day?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Did you see any other airplanes in the sky on that day, during the attack?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, the sounds that we've just heard now, other than what appears to be the sounds of the motor of the airplane, could you tell the Trial Chamber what they were.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: The sounds that were heard just now, is that right?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, to me it sounds like shooting, gunfire from what I was able to discern.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, for the record, the witness is referring to still on the video -- from the video which is at 27 minutes, 59.9 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And are those sounds of gunfire similar to the sounds of gunfire that you heard during the attack in your village that day?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Are those sounds of gunfire, the sounds of gunfire you've just testified about, did they sound like the gunfire you heard that day in your village while it was under attack?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I was able to hear, this was like gunfire.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, you see smoke at the bottom centre of this screen. Could you tell the Trial Chamber whether that is smoke that is coming from the fire, from your village, or from another source?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: No. The smoke seen at the bottom of the screen is the house in Serbia, and the smoke that you can see in the far end, in the background, that's from across the river Drina.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In fact, Ms. Sellers, I don't know, you probably have noticed but when we started rolling this video, where that fire is, it was already there at the beginning and there was a gentleman, a man standing nearby.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I want to make it clear for the record, we won't be misleading since it looks very similar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So it is good to point out that this is Serbia and not across the Drina.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. One moment. This is, for the record, we are -- the witness was being referred to a clip or a still from the video at 28 minutes, 28.7 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Petrovic, from your experience, would you tell the Trial Chamber where is this video -- where does this video appear to be taken from, as we're looking at the village of Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: I think from Serbia. There's no other place.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now you've testified that between your village and Serbia, there is the Drina River. Is that indicated in the image that we're seeing before us now on the screen?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, the Drina is here, you can see it here on this image.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you. We will note the time for that one also, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. For the record, the witness is referring to a still from the video at 28 minutes 46.9 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we're going to fast-forward to one time period, if you would allow us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Turn it back for one minute. Now, Mr. Petrovic, you've testified about two, what appears to be sections of houses that were burned one above the road and one below the road in Bjelovac. Could you indicate for the Trial Chamber if what is on the screen now represents one of those groups of houses and, if so, which group of houses. Below the road or above the road?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: I think that this other, the second part is below the road. And there is another portion, I think it's probably Jovanovici, further up towards the wooded area. Because you can see the Drina River and the house that is on fire is right next to the river.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you. We will note the time for that also Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And for the record, the still that the witness is referring to occurs at 32 minutes 33 seconds point 4.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: We will go directly to one other segment. [Videotape played].

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Petrovic, I would ask you to look at this image in front of you and, could you please tell the Trial Chamber if you know what part of the village of Bjelovac does this image represent.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: This is the part just below the road and near the Drina River, between the road and the river.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. For the record, the witness is referring to a still at 38 minutes, 15.1 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we can stop the video at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's up to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Petrovic, did you have a chance to go back into your village in the following months in which it was attacked?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, I returned to Bjelovac for the first time sometime in March, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Were you part of the Serb army forces that went back into Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, were you in the front troops or were you in the rear troops of those forces that went into Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: After the fall of Bjelovac, a unit was established in Bratunac and I belonged to it. It was the 2nd Company, 3rd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And when you went back into the town of Bjelovac, would you please describe for the Trial Chamber what you observed in the town.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: When we returned to Bjelovac, the houses had all been burned down. That was in March, when we retook the village, our village.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now when you stated that houses had all been burned down, are you referring to those that burned down on the 14th of December as well as those that burned down on the 17th of December?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, all the houses in Bjelovac. Only four Muslim houses remained untouched. They had not been burned.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now when you say four Muslim houses, did you know that the inhabitants of that -- those houses were Muslims?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: I knew my next door neighbour, Hajrudin Begzadic, that was the house, two houses away from my house.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now would you describe for the Trial Chamber what Hajrudin's house looked like when you returned in March compared to the other houses.

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, when we returned there in March, there were quite a few things around his house, cement mixers, chain saws, that people had gathered there around his house. It looked like a storage facility, as a warehouse.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, when you say people had gathered had you seen any people between the time you left your village until the time you returned to your village, gathering things in the village and placing them near Hajrudin's house?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well since I was there quite close in Grabovica, I did not see them leave the stuff next to Hajrudin's house, but I did see quite a few people moving around in Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And were these people dressed as civilians or in uniforms or a combination of both?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, I really could not see that, because it's -- the distance was quite substantial.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: When you spoke with your former Serb neighbours, did they ever tell you that they had taken things or items and gathered them at Hajrudin's house during this time period?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: When we returned to Bjelovac, people who would recognise their cement mixer or digger would say, "this is mine," and took those things. Now as to whether this really belonged to them or not, I cannot go into that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, the other three Muslim houses, what condition were they in, compared to the non-Muslim houses and did they also have items stored around them?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, there were some items, less than at Hajrudin's place. Those houses had not been burned because even when the Serbs were there, Serbs lived in them. And then, when Muslims came, they all returned to their houses, the houses of the Muslims, and thus it happened that nobody ever set fire to those houses and the houses remained there unscathed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, were there any vehicles such as cars or trucks or tractors that were missing in the village after you returned?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: In Bjelovac, there was nothing. In my garage, there was a yellow Zastava 101 car. It was my son in law's. This car was gone and we found two cars that were burned further down the road in Bjelovac, on the black top road.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Did your Serb neighbours also tell you whether they had vehicles, cars or tractors that were missing after the attack on Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, there were no vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just have two more questions and I will end this session, okay?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, on the 17th you testified that the rest of Bjelovac, that had not been burned on the 14th, was burned. To your knowledge, were there any village guards or Serb soldiers defending Bjelovac on that day?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: No. Everything was taken out of Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't think that that is an answer to the question that you put, it could be a question of interpretation. I suggest you put the question again.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Everyone had been pulled out the village.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter apologises. The answer was slightly ambiguous.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: So therefore on the 17th of December, 1992, was Bjelovac an undefended town, in terms of being defended by Serb soldiers or Serb civilians?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: I think it was on the 17th that the remaining people pulled out of Bjelovac. Everyone was pulled out on the 17th of December and no Serbs remained there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And when you saw the fires being set on the 17th of December, from your position in Serbia, did you hear any shooting or any defending of the town simultaneous to the houses being burned?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: He said -- I think the witness didn't say he saw fires being set.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You are right, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, he saw -- he -- let me not mischaracterise his testimony. He said he "saw houses burning."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I will rephrase that in terms. During -- on the 17th of December, from your vantage point in Serbia, when you saw houses burning in that part of the town, Bjelovac, did you also hear gun fighting or hear the town being defended by Serb soldiers or Serb inhabitants?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA PETROVIC
utterances.text: No. No. You could just see the fires. There was no shooting.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I will finish and I will inform the Trial Chamber I have no more than 10 minutes for tomorrow morning, 10 or 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I don't know. I think one should prepare the witness as to the chances of him having to stay here over the weekend and continue and finish on Monday. But, I don't know, it's up to you. We will continue tomorrow in the afternoon, like today. And hopefully we will not need to send you in and out and bring you in again in order to discuss procedural matters. We will do our utmost, our best to try and finish tomorrow. I don't promise you that we will because we lost too much time today discussing procedural problems that were raised. Have a nice evening. Rest. And tomorrow we will continue. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: be reconvened on Friday, the 15th day of April, 2005, at 2.15 p.m.
